function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Where to Find More Detail | |-------|---------|---------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 45 mph on urban interstates,
• 35 mph on city streets (unless posted otherwise).
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if a school bus is present). | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001–545.004 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021, 545.022 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Stop signs and red lights must be obeyed. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021–545.023 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop sign extended.
• Cannot pass a stopped school bus until the lights stop flashing and the sign retracts. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Lane Discipline** | • Do not drive in the wrong lane or in a lane marked for turning unless turning.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, 15 ft of a stop sign, or 30 ft of a railroad crossing.
• Parking on a shoulder is prohibited unless marked. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for parking violations, abandoned vehicles, or if they pose a hazard.
• The towing company must notify the owner and the police. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021–545.023 | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Special Rules for Motorcycles & Bicycles** | • Motorcyclists must wear helmets.
• Bicyclists must use bike lanes where available and obey traffic signals. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021–545.023 | | **Electronic Toll Collection** | • Texas uses the TxTag system for toll roads. | TxTag website | | **Recent Updates (2024)** | • Texas introduced a “Safe Driving” program encouraging safe driving habits.
• New penalties for texting while driving were enacted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) news releases | --- ### How to Get Official Texts 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – For registration, insurance, and driver’s license information: https://www.txdmv.gov/ 3. **TxDOT** – For road conditions, construction, and safety programs: https://www.txdot.gov/ 4. **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection** – For updates on DUI laws and enforcement: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ --- ### Quick Tips for Texas Drivers - **Always check posted speed limits** – they can change at construction zones or school zones. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on your phone. - **Keep a safe following distance** – at least 2 seconds behind the vehicle in front. - **Be extra cautious at school zones** – children may be present at any time. - **Know your insurance limits** – they must meet the state minimums. Feel free to ask if you need more specific details on any of these topics!
